Spotify key metrics — marketplace mix, ARPU, cash, multiple

SPOT-zbar-2026-09-21 · EUR · series 2026-09-30T18:50:00Z · built 2026-09-30 18:47 UTC

The short version

Own SPOT for three to ten years. An audio marketplace at global scale — not a music-rights bet, and not a software multiple waiting for agentic AI to erase headphones.

SPOT · EUR ops / USD price · as of 2026-09-30 (ET) · CLEAR week ending 2026-09-20

Spotify runs one front door into paid subscriptions (Premium) and ads on the free tier (Ad-Supported). Premium is the dollar core; Ad-Supported is the funnel and the smaller absolute line. Premium and Ad-Supported users overlap — they are not two pieces of one total. In the second quarter of 2026 the company printed €4.78B revenue (€4.33B Premium / €446M Ad), operating income €655M, net income €545M, and free cash flow €797M.

Growth in the dollars is price-and-mix inside Premium (ARPU €4.89 vs €4.57 a year earlier) while paid subscriber year-over-year cooled to +8.7%. The faster funnel is Ad-Supported monthly active users (+14.1% to 494M). Total monthly active users held a mid-teens-to-low-teens band (+11.6% to 777M). Podcast and audiobook hours as a share of listening stay blank in the public record — we do not invent them.

Major risks

  • Sustained multi-quarter decay in monthly active users or listening — not one soft print
  • Operating margin stepping down quarter after quarter without a clear reinvestment story
  • Premium growth stall sold as “all mix” while ARPU rolls over
  • Ad-Supported funnel stall while the Premium mix story continues

Close competitors

  • Apple Music — hardware/OS bundle; thinner ad-funnel exposure
  • YouTube Music / Google — attention and ads at search/video scale
  • Amazon Music — Prime attach and commerce bundle
  • Podcast hosts / digital audio ads — free-tier ad dollars and exclusive talent
